meta: AI can be wrong and still sound very sure, and children tend to believe it. Three habits help kids check AI: ask for sources, compare with textbooks, and play spot-the-mistake.

muc.title: AI is wrong, but confident
muc.text: AI can say something wrong in a very confident voice, and children tend to believe it right away.

muc.title: Ask where it got that
muc.text: Teach your child the first habit: ask AI where this information comes from, then open that source to see if it's real.

muc.title: Compare with the textbook
muc.text: The second habit: compare with the textbook or ask the teacher, and note down anything that differs to ask about.

muc.title: A spot-the-mistake game
muc.text: Turn it into a game: every evening, find one mistake AI makes together, and whoever catches it gets a point.

muc.title: Catch a mistake tonight
muc.text: Tonight, ask AI a question about where you live, like a local specialty dish or a school's name, then check together whether it's right.
